name: shosa
description: Write human movement as text and watch it performed beside the source.
author: Yoshifumi Tsuda

commands.title: Shosa: Open Preview to the Side
Export Model File (glTF, VRM Animation, BVH)…

languageModelTools.name: shosa_grammar
languageModelTools.userDescription: The whole Shosa language, so the assistant can write .shosa files (character movement as text).
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the complete grammar of Shosa, a language in which the movement of a humanoid character (a dance, an attack combo, an idle, a gesture, a walk) is written as text in a .shosa file and compiled to an animation (glTF, VRM Animation, BVH). Shosa is new and you do not know it: ALWAYS call this once before you write or change any .shosa file, or answer a question about the language, and read all of it. A word that is not in it does not exist; never guess. The result ends with how to work in this editor (tools shosa_check and shosa_sheet). Takes no input.

languageModelTools.name: shosa_check
languageModelTools.userDescription: Compiles a .shosa file: its problems, and every score with its length, sections, tempo and marks.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Compiles a .shosa file (Shosa: character movement as text) as the editor has it, saved or not, and returns what the compiler says: a line 'FILE(line,column): severity CODE: message' for each problem, or 'no problems'; then every score with its beats, seconds and dancers, each section with its beats, bars, seconds, tempo and time, and every mark (!hit) with its beat and second. Call it after EVERY change to a .shosa file and fix until it says 'no problems'. Take lengths and times from this report instead of computing them. To know how the body is turned at a moment (hips, shoulders and face, in degrees from the way the feet face; how far each elbow and knee is bent), pass 'at' instead of computing angles from joint positions. If you have not read the grammar in this conversation, call shosa_grammar first.

file.description: The .shosa file: its full path, or its path from the workspace folder.

score.description: The name of the one score to report (as this tool lists them). Without it, every score.

at.description: Moments to say how each dancer's body is turned at: beats, or seconds with an s, with commas between ("3,4.5" or "0.75s"). The same as `shosa check FILE --at`.

languageModelTools.name: shosa_sheet
languageModelTools.userDescription: Draws the movement of a .shosa file as an image: a pose per beat and the floor from above.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Draws the movement a .shosa file compiles to and returns it as an image for you to look at: for each score, the figures' pose at every beat from left to right (left limbs blue, right limbs red) and their path over the floor from above. Call it after shosa_check says 'no problems', and LOOK at the image of every score you changed: no diagnostics does not mean the right movement. A file with several scores returns an image for each; pass 'score' for one. Movement shorter than a beat falls between the poses: pass 'step' (0.25 or 0.5) with 'from' and 'to'. A punch, a kick or a bow straight ahead does not show from the front: pass 'view': 'side'.

file.description: The .shosa file: its full path, or its path from the workspace folder.

score.description: The name of the one score to draw (as shosa_check lists them). Without it, every score.

step.description: Beats between two poses. Without it, one beat (three in 6/8, 9/8 and 12/8).

from.description: The beat to begin at, or seconds as a string with an s ("0.5s"). Without it, 0.

to.description: The beat to end at, or seconds as a string with an s ("1s"). Without it, the end of the score.

view.description: 'front' (the default, a little from the side), 'side' (from stage left: a figure facing front is seen in profile), 'back', or degrees round from the front.

shosa.server.path.description: Path to Shosa.Lsp.dll. Empty uses the server shipped with the extension, or the one built in this repository.

shosa.playback.soundFont.markdownDescription: The sound font the preview plays a dance's song with: a path to an `.sf2`, `.sf3` or `.dls` file on this machine. Empty: the one Lily# plays with — its `lilysharp.playback.soundFont` setting, else the font of the *Lily# Sound Font* extension when that is installed, else the General MIDI bank of the operating system. Where there is none, the preview plays simple tones.
